result.question: Fill gaps from a prior survey of A2A (Agent2Agent protocol) SDKs, as of late 2026. Already known (do not re-research): official Python/Go/Java/JS SDKs target spec v1.0, support JSON-RPC/REST/gRPC; Python TaskStore/PushNotificationConfigStore/ClientFactory details; Java Extras JPA stores and ReplicatedQueueManager. Research ONLY these gaps: (1) Official a2a-dotnet SDK (github.com/a2aproject/a2a-dotnet, NuGet A2A / A2A.AspNetCore): current version, spec v1.0 conformance, supported transports, task store and push abstractions, agent card signing, extended card, ASP.NET Core hosting integration (MapA2A etc.), client API, telemetry, known gaps/issues. (2) Framework integrations: Google ADK (to_a2a, RemoteA2aAgent), Microsoft Agent Framework / Semantic Kernel A2A hosting and A2AAgent client, LangGraph/LangSmith server A2A endpoint, BeeAI/Agent Stack — do they build on official SDKs or reimplement, what hosting patterns they add. (3) A2A TCK (a2a-tck): what it tests, how SDKs wire it into CI, which SDKs pass v1.0. (4) OpenTelemetry in A2A SDKs: span names, attributes, trace context propagation across streaming and push notifications (e.g. a2a-python a2a.utils.telemetry, Java OTel extra). (5) Server-side agent card signing (JWS, JWKS, canonicalization per spec) and authenticated extended agent card implementations across SDKs; resubscribe/subscribe-to-task implementation outside Java. Goal: inform design of a .NET A2A SDK; highlight patterns to copy and gaps.
result.summary: The official a2a-dotnet SDK (NuGet packages A2A, A2A.AspNetCore, A2A.Grpc, A2A.Grpc.AspNetCore) is still prerelease. The latest version is 1.0.0-preview4, released 2026-11-02, and there is no stable 1.0 yet. It says it implements spec v1.0, and a separate A2A.V0_3 package keeps v0.3 compatibility. It supports three transports, JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON REST with SSE, and gRPC, through one IA2AClient contract and one IA2ARequestHandler server pipeline. gRPC is optional and ships as separate packages, so core users do not depend on Grpc.*. ASP.NET Core hosting uses AddA2AAgent<THandler>(), MapA2A(), MapHttpA2A(), MapWellKnownAgentCard() and AddA2AGrpc()/MapGrpcA2A(). Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET and Python) builds on the official SDKs and does not reimplement them. It adds a keyed, per-agent hosting layer with replaceable stores, but it serves only HTTP+JSON and JSON-RPC and does not support background tasks yet. LangSmith Agent Server serves a partial v1.0 JSON-RPC endpoint with no SubscribeToTask and no push notifications. No verified evidence survived on several gaps: the TCK, OpenTelemetry conventions, server-side card signing (JWS/JWKS), extended card implementations, Google ADK, BeeAI, and the a2a-dotnet task store and push abstractions. Those gaps are still open.

findings.claim: a2a-dotnet targets A2A spec v1.0, and a separate A2A.V0_3 NuGet package plus an A2A.V0_3Compat layer give v0.3 backward compatibility during the transition. The README tells v0.3 clients that call a v1 server to set configuration.blocking=true.
findings.evidence: The README on GitHub and the README on each NuGet package say 'This library implements the A2A v1.0 specification.' The sample card sets ProtocolVersion = 1.0. This is the project's own claim, not proof of a TCK pass.

findings.claim: All a2a-dotnet packages are prerelease. A2A, A2A.AspNetCore and A2A.Grpc are all at 1.0.0-preview4 (2026-11-02). Earlier versions: preview3 (2026-10-14), preview2 (2026-04-09), preview (2026-03-16) and 0.3.x previews. There is no stable release. A2A.AspNetCore targets net8.0, is compatible with net10.0, and depends on A2A >= 1.0.0-preview4.
findings.evidence: NuGet version tables. Preview2 has about 547k downloads, so most users are on it. Preview4 is one day old.

findings.claim: a2a-dotnet supports three transports: JSON-RPC, HTTP+JSON REST with SSE streaming, and gRPC with server streaming. All three share one client contract (IA2AClient) and one server pipeline (IA2ARequestHandler, implemented by A2AServer). gRPC ships as two optional packages, A2A.Grpc (client) and A2A.Grpc.AspNetCore (server), so core users do not take a Grpc.* dependency. This is a good pattern to copy.
findings.evidence: README Protocol Compatibility section: 'All three bindings share the same IA2AClient contract and IA2ARequestHandler server pipeline.'

findings.claim: ASP.NET Core hosting API: AddA2AAgent<THandler>() registers the agent, its card and its services in DI. MapA2A() maps JSON-RPC, MapHttpA2A() maps REST, and MapWellKnownAgentCard() serves discovery. AddA2AGrpc() and MapGrpcA2A() live in A2A.Grpc.AspNetCore. MapGrpcA2A mirrors MapA2A/MapHttpA2A and reuses the same agent registration and handler pipeline. gRPC can run alongside the JSON-RPC/HTTP endpoints or replace them.
findings.evidence: API inventory in the README and the NuGet READMEs, with sample code builder.Services.AddA2AGrpc(); app.MapGrpcA2A().

findings.claim: Client API: A2AClient (the main client), A2ACardResolver, and A2AGrpcClient (an IA2AClient with parity for all unary and streaming calls). A2AClientFactory.Create(agentCard) picks a binding using PreferredBindings (ProtocolBindingNames.Grpc, etc.). gRPC must be registered first with A2AGrpcClientRegistration.Register(). gRPC faults surface as A2AException with an A2AErrorCode.
findings.evidence: The README describes the binding registration and factory selection, and shows sample code using PreferredBindings = [ProtocolBindingNames.Grpc].

findings.claim: Microsoft Agent Framework (.NET) builds A2A hosting on the official a2a-dotnet SDK and does not reimplement the protocol. Microsoft.Agents.AI.Hosting.A2A.AspNetCore pulls in the SDK packages. MapWellKnownAgentCard comes from the SDK's A2A.AspNetCore. Cards use the SDK's AgentCard, AgentInterface and ProtocolBindingNames. ITaskManager is no longer exposed; an IAgentHandler is resolved internally instead.
findings.evidence: Note in the docs: '`MapWellKnownAgentCard` is provided by the A2A SDK package (`A2A.AspNetCore`), not the Agent Framework hosting packages.'

findings.claim: MAF .NET hosting pattern: builder.AddA2AServer(name) registers a keyed A2AServer singleton per agent. app.MapA2AHttpJson(name, path) and app.MapA2AJsonRpc(name, path) map endpoints, and both can run at once. These replace the removed MapA2A overloads, and A2AHostingOptions was renamed A2AServerRegistrationOptions. Defaults: IAgentHandler=A2AAgentHandler, AgentSessionStore=InMemoryAgentSessionStore, ITaskStore=InMemoryTaskStore, AgentRunMode=DisallowBackground. You override them with keyed DI services registered before AddA2AServer (AgentRunMode is set through options instead). The in-memory stores are for development only. Limits: no gRPC, no background (task) responses yet, and one card per host at the well-known path. The client defaults to HTTP+JSON and falls back to JSON-RPC.
findings.evidence: The Microsoft Learn docs have tables of defaults, override samples using AddKeyedSingleton, and the migration quick-reference table. The keyed-per-agent DI pattern is worth copying.

findings.claim: MAF moved its C# and Python A2A packages from A2A SDK v0.3 to v1. This was a breaking change for both the client (A2AAgent) and hosting packages. In Python, agent-framework-a2a's A2AExecutor implements the a2a-sdk AgentExecutor, maps the A2A context ID to an Agent Framework session, and publishes status and artifact events through the SDK's TaskUpdater. It is used with the SDK's DefaultRequestHandler, InMemoryTaskStore and create_jsonrpc_routes. agent-framework-hosting-a2a adds AgentA2AAdapter and WorkflowA2AAdapter.
findings.evidence: Docs: 'Both packages use native A2A SDK types and server components.' The C# client wraps SDK types through A2AClient.AsAIAgent().

findings.claim: LangSmith Agent Server exposes an A2A endpoint per assistant at /a2a/{assistant_id}, with the card at /.well-known/agent-card.json?assistant_id=. It supports only the v1.0 JSON-RPC binding; gRPC and REST are not implemented. Supported methods: SendMessage, SendStreamingMessage (SSE), GetTask, CancelTask, ListTasks and GetExtendedAgentCard. SubscribeToTask and the push-config methods are not implemented, and unknown methods return -32601. Only four v0.3 method names are accepted (message/send, message/stream, tasks/get, tasks/cancel), so tasks/resubscribe and agent/getAuthenticatedExtendedCard fail.
findings.evidence: Single vendor doc, but primary and current. It says verbatim: 'Only the JSON-RPC binding is available.' and 'Exactly four v0.3 names are accepted'. The docs do not say whether LangSmith builds on a2a-python or reimplements it.

result.caveats: Every a2a-dotnet package is a preview (1.0.0-preview4, one day old), so API names may change before GA. 'Implements v1.0' is a README claim, not a TCK result. Nearly all evidence is from vendor or official docs, and the LangSmith finding rests on one page. Several research gaps produced no verified claims: the a2a-dotnet ITaskStore and push-notification abstractions, agent card signing, extended card, telemetry and open issues; Google ADK (to_a2a, RemoteA2aAgent); BeeAI/Agent Stack; the a2a-tck scope, CI wiring and v1.0 pass status; OpenTelemetry span names, attributes and propagation; server-side JWS/JWKS card signing; and subscribe/resubscribe outside Java. Treat them as unknown, not as absent. Two claims about the community a2a-net package (WebSocket hosting, AddA2AProtocolServer) were refuted 0-3. The MAF docs wrongly say A2A has only two bindings, but gRPC is part of v1.0.
openQuestions: What task store, push-notification config store and push sender abstractions does a2a-dotnet expose? Does it ship durable stores or only in-memory ones?
Does a2a-dotnet (or any SDK) do server-side agent card signing with JWS, JCS canonicalization and JWKS, and does it support an authenticated extended agent card on the server?
What does a2a-tck test for v1.0, how do the official SDKs (including dotnet) run it in CI, and which ones pass?
What OpenTelemetry span names, attributes and trace-context propagation do the SDKs use across SSE streaming and push notifications, and does a2a-dotnet emit ActivitySource spans?

refuted.claim: a2a-net hosts A2A over JSON-RPC 2.0, using WebSocket and HTTP endpoints. The page does not mention REST or gRPC transports.
The ASP.NET Core hosting pattern uses AddA2AProtocolServer with a builder, plus separate MapA2AAgentHttpEndpoint and MapA2AAgentWebSocketEndpoint route mappings.
